title: Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2018
short_title: Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prohibit live animal exports for slaughter from 1 July 2021 and impose interim welfare requirements on livestock exporters before that date.
Exporters would need to take reasonable steps to ensure satisfactory treatment overseas, including specified holding, transport and slaughter standards and stunning before slaughter.
The legislation would begin on Royal Assent, with transitional exemptions available in certain cases involving contracts made before commencement and the permanent ban starting later.
changes: Export licences would cease to authorise livestock exports for slaughter from 1 July 2021.
Exporters would have to notify the Secretary within 14 days if satisfactory overseas treatment had not occurred.
Interim export approvals would require the Secretary to be satisfied about welfare treatment or an applicable transitional exemption.
summary.affected: Livestock export licence holders and live animals exported for slaughter are affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Wilkie
speeches.brief: The Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2018 would end all live sheep and cattle exports from Australia by 2021 with interim tougher safeguards, citing systemic cruelty (e.g., over 2,000 sheep deaths on the Awassi Express) and arguing the industry is not in Australia's economic interest, damages its reputation, and lacks public support.
